shots.prompt: Photorealistic candid photo, vertical framing. A plain university seminar room on a grey overcast afternoon: flat daylight from windows on the left, fluorescent ceiling panels, beige walls, a ceiling projector switched off. A wide white whiteboard spans the front wall across the full width of the frame, in the upper half. The whiteboard is completely full, edge to edge, of handwritten dry-erase marker in black, blue and red. Copy everything written on the attached reference board exactly, character for character, with the same layout: the equations, the spring-and-mass sketch at the top right and the cosine graph at the bottom left. Large, roomy writing at the top left, smaller and tighter toward the bottom right, the last lines squeezed tiny into the bottom-right corner and two lines written sideways up the right edge. Written in a real person's marker hand, not a font. A male teacher in his mid 40s, short dark hair going grey, rolled-up light blue shirt sleeves, stands at the right end of the board in three-quarter view, bent slightly at the knees, pressing a black marker into the last free corner of the board, trying to squeeze in one more line, his brow furrowed. Out-of-focus empty student desks along the bottom edge of the frame. All four corners of the whiteboard in frame, the writing sharp. No other text, no logos. Adults only: the students are university students in their twenties, no children or teenagers anywhere, and the room is a plain university seminar room, not a school classroom: no school decorations, posters, children's artwork, cubbies or small desks.
shots.why: The teacher and the whiteboard he's run out of, as one real-looking moment: the strain of squeezing the last line in is what code can't make believable. The maths on the board is copied from board-ref.png, a correct derivation built in code, and is checked line by line before the video is made from it.
